_: The HelloBuh shared world: one seed, every place at ONE canonical spot (docs/world/canon.md). lib/world.js builds places from here; never search for a site. Days are the world timeline (day 0 = the world was made). Pieces: lib/sets pieces with canonical x, y, z, facing, variant (y measured from the survey: scripts/world_survey.py). Stamps: small fixed operations (cmds, summon, setblock, fill, sign, frame); live: re-summoned every run. since/until: the days it exists.

hub.title: The Green: where the stories happen

the_green.name: The Green
the_green.about: The green island on the east coast between the White and the sea: forest rim, the High Meadow plateau (y 115-123), the North Inlet, the Lava Field. Almost every story happens here.

the_white.name: The White
the_white.about: Two kilometres of snowy plains, ice spikes and frozen rivers between the Green and the West March. Snowy villages, igloos, two ancient cities deep under it.

the_west_march.name: The West March
the_west_march.about: Green coast country west of the White: Ravenford, the Ridge and its outpost, the stronghold under the islets.

hushwell.name: Hushwell

vanilla.note: the seed generates it: nothing to build, never /place it again

hushwell.about: Buh's home village on a terrace above the east coast; the hill north-west of it is Dog Hill. The well (its centre is the origin) sits over a shrieker (Light Sleeper's staging: the ancient city under it is the story's, the seed's nearest are 1,200 blocks west). Carpeted from day 1400 until Buh stops playing (day 3400): shriekers only answer players.

stamps.what: the village bell in a two-post frame, boxed in white wool, open to the west (Light Sleeper's, kept boxed for good)

dog_hill.name: Dog Hill
dog_hill.about: The flat hilltop north-west of Hushwell, 29 blocks above the plaza (as Dog on the Hill built it; its bible's layout differs, the render is canon): Buh's childhood dirt hut north-east of D, the patch where he logged out (D + (3, 0, 0)), and the dog on D facing it, since day 3400.

stamps.what: the hilltop meadow as Dog on the Hill built it: a disc (r 9) round D levelled to y 108, a grassy ridge rising to the west, a mound to the south-east, mossy boulders, leaf bushes, a birch, two oaks, low flowers (same seed); the dog's spot worn to coarse dirt
Buh's 5x5 dirt hut north-east of D (D + (3..7, 1..4, -8..-4)), oak door south toward the patch, a torch, crafting table and furnace, moss, vines, a cobweb
the worn path step below the south rim with two lanterns on posts (where Hushwell's grandpa stands)
the patch P = D + (3, 0, 0): the one clean grass block where Buh logged out
the dog: a pale wolf, tamed (Owner: the recording player, Buh), red collar (CollarColor 14), sitting on D facing east at the patch and the village
cmds: /execute as @p run data modify entity @e[tag=dog,limit=1,sort=nearest] Owner set from entity @s UUID

stamps.what: the pile of 14 bones beside him, never eaten
Pip (a baby plains villager) sitting on the dog's right (D + (0, 0, 1)), nights only

fernbank.name: Fernbank
fernbank.about: The riverside village on the east bank of the North Inlet, 60 blocks west of the Lava Field. The old tales happen here: the creeper's village party (Runaway), the nitwit who stands where bad things happen (Nitwit), the respawns that cost a villager each (Respawn Tax). Empty but for the librarian and the iron golem from day 520.

stamps.what: the fisherman's boat, empty, tied at the dock end (he jumped in it in Runaway; Respawn Tax found it floating)
the iron golem, standing on the librarian's respawn line by the well
the librarian, the last villager in Fernbank, at her door
the last torch on the south road (past it: the Burned Copy)

burned_copy.name: The Burned Copy
burned_copy.about: Past the last torch south of Fernbank: a burned, empty copy of Fernbank's north row (the nitwit's world, which already ended). Same pieces and seeds as Fernbank's, charred.

stamps.what: char it: planks and logs to blackened blocks, glass and wool gone, no lights

digger_house.name: The Digger's House
digger_house.about: A birch cottage on the lowland under the High Meadow's east slope, the inlet behind it. Its owner digs straight down, dies, and forgets: Torch Hill behind the house is full of one-wide shafts, each under a torch or a dirt block.

stamps.what: Torch Hill: a torch on the slope behind the house, and under it a one-wide shaft 40 deep with a torch every 4 blocks on the left wall
the dirt block the blue sheep stares at, with a line of torches from the door
the hole where the sheep's block was (Sheep Stares): straight down
the blue sheep, staring at the block

stillwater.name: Stillwater
stillwater.about: A small farming village on the north shore. The Long Day happened here (days 800-1100: the lever froze the sun for the whole world). The night it ended the zombies under the one tree came out; Gary the farmer was taken that night, and has walked out of the fog to his own field every night since.

stamps.what: the one tree the zombies hid under through the Long Day
the Long Day lever on a stone post in the square (pulled back since day 1100)
Gary: a zombie villager farmer (straw hat), name tag "Gary", at the fog line by his field; nights only

cliff_house.name: The Cliff House
cliff_house.about: A family house on the west rim of the High Meadow, a 40-block fall to the White's frozen shore below. Respawn Voice's family: a brother, a sister, Dad, the new bed.

tidewater.name: Tidewater
tidewater.about: Lowland fishing hamlet one block above the sea, south of Hushwell, with a lighthouse on the rise. One Block Higher happens here: the sea creeping in, the villagers digging.

saltmouth.name: Saltmouth
saltmouth.about: The village on the south peninsula (survey start (-286, -381); Good Boy's set measures from (-304, -384)). Buh lived here with the dog at 16, in the cottage on the pad above the south-east shore (Good Boy). From day 3450 a family's stilt house stands on the boardwalk under that bank with the village bell on a belfry outside his window (The Bell in the Window, day 3800).

stamps.what: Buh's yard and cottage on the pad at village + (29..44, 9..33), the village origin being Good Boy's (-304, -384): level grass at y 70 whose south-east corner stands 8 blocks over the sea on a stepped bank (Good Boy's "cliff"), the spruce-fenced yard, the cottage, the fancy oak (-273, 71, -353) and the old oak (-261, 71, -353) on the bank's corner. Ported verbatim from stunts/story_good_boy.js (the pad, the cottage, the yard, its trees; the trees are /place feature, so their shape varies a little per build; the wheat field west of it is still the stunt's). The pad buried the ruined portal at (-269, -366). Empty from day 3400: no dog, no Buh, the chimney cold

Buh's yard after he left: the chimney's campfire out, the eight lanterns (gate posts, yard, cottage) gone dark (removed). Through day 3400 (Good Boy, which builds with day 3400) the yard is lit as Good Boy built it

the Bell in the Window family's two-storey stilt house on a plank boardwalk over the sea under Buh's yard's south-east bank: its north wall at z -340, his upstairs window (1 x 2, y 66-67) at x -263 facing north at the bank, a porch roof (walking surface y 66) east of it, the upstairs door east at O + (4, 4, 2), the boardwalk at y 62. Inside 7 x 7 on both floors (the owner's interior minimum); the ground floor is y 63-64, the upstairs floor y 65. Origin O = (-263, 62, -340), bell_window's set-relative (0, 0, 0). The bell set's live gate may move it in half-blocks

Saltmouth's meeting-point bell re-hung on a two-post belfry 3 north of his window, O + (0, 7, -3) = (-263, 69, -343), double_wall between oak-fence posts capped with oak logs, on a cobblestone base, nothing above it. The bell that catches the skeleton's arrows (an arrow sticks in it a minute, then despawns)

the pale guy: a skeleton in the old oak's shade on Buh's yard's south-east bank, feet O + (0, 9, -12) = (-262.5, 71, -351.5), bow, facing his window. Moved in about 100 days after Buh left (300 nights before day 3800). After day 3800 never shown (the Short ends on the draw)

frostgate.name: Frostgate
frostgate.about: The snowy village at the White's east edge, on the old road west. More Golems happens here (19 golems, 6 villagers).

ravenford.name: Ravenford
ravenford.about: Grandpa's village across the White, 2 km west of Hushwell: the log palisade and its east gate (the origin), Grandpa's house and yard just inside it with the totem wall (32 full from raid 32), the shepherd family's pasture south of the gate (blue sheep from raid 32: the evoker alarm), the road east over the ford and up onto the Ridge. A real pillager outpost stands 200 blocks further east, the stronghold 250 blocks west under the low headland past Leo's lagoon (Gullwick).

pieces.note: the old tower on the hill: Thirty-One Raids builds it here (gate O + (44, 40))

stamps.what: Grandpa's house and yard just inside the east gate (gate + (-18..-3, -19..-2)): cobblestone and spruce, door south at x -10, two south windows (x -13, -7) and one east; the bench, grindstone, lantern post and fence of the yard. Ported verbatim from stunts/story_thirty_one_raids.js grandpaHouse() and its yard (that stunt still builds its own copy)

the totem wall after raid 32: all 32 frames full (4 rows of 8 on the north wall inside, gate + (-13..-6, 3..6, -16); frame 32 a glow frame), the four bottle frames by the east window, the bowl, and the sign under it (RAIDS WON 32). Seen from outside through the south windows (x -13 and -7). Before day 1900 the wall is Thirty-One Raids' own (30, then 31, of 32)

the shepherd family's pasture inside the palisade south of the east gate: an oak fence on the natural ground round gate + (-29..-1, 13..40), the palisade its east side with the pasture gate in it at gate + (0, 15), a lantern on the corner post. The flock in it is dyed blue from raid 32 on (Red Sheep)
eight of Ravenford's blue sheep (Color 11) in the pasture: the evoker alarm (a blue sheep in an evoker's 16 blocks turns red). Red Sheep brings its own 60

Seventy Below: the room under Grandpa's house and yard, air x -2058..-2050, y 65..67, z -501..-489, stone floor y 64 and walls, ceiling y 68 (the house's cobblestone foundation under the house, stone under the yard). The seventy zombies are story-only (summoned by the stunt), not stamped.
Seventy Below: the 1x1 shaft from the room's ceiling to the yard at x -2057, z -492 (air y 68..70), its lid the yard's own grass block at y 71 (looks like the rest of the yard)
Seventy Below: Grandpa's red bed, head north at (-2058, 73, -500) against the bookshelf column, foot (-2058, 73, -499)

ravenford.story_builds: the palisade and the east gate are still built by stunts/story_thirty_one_raids.js (gate-relative, on the terrain); Grandpa's house, yard and the totem wall are ported here (stamps). Port the palisade before the next Ravenford story builds (Red Sheep's set.md)

leo_house.name: Leo's House
leo_house.about: A stone cottage on the shore west of Ravenford, facing a lagoon and, across it, the low headland over the real stronghold (Gullwick stands on it from day ~350; the survey found no islet over the stronghold). Leo left for the End six years before One More Eye; the basement holds an end portal frame that gains an eye a night.

portal_cottage.name: The Portal Cottage
portal_cottage.about: A spruce cottage on the hill's south-east slope north of Hushwell, looking south-south-west down the slope to Hushwell's plaza. The cellar under it has a lit Nether portal in its east wall; the grandson's grandpa walked into it on day ~175 and never came back. The cellar's hatch is in the cottage floor by the bed, down a ladder shaft; years of barters (obsidian, crying obsidian, soul sand) patch its walls.

stamps.what: the slope below the garden kept clear of trees (Grandma's view down to Hushwell)

oakend.name: Oakend
oakend.about: A cleric's hamlet on the North Inlet's west bank, facing Fernbank across the water: a lane of cottages east of an oak fence and its west gate, and a meadow that climbs west from the gate to a dark oak treeline. Every villager wears a name tag. A siege (~day 2500) converted Tomas, Greta and Old Ben, whose cottages stand shut; on day 2700 their cleric, Rosa, is converted at dusk and her son Remy, the hamlet's only player, throws the cure.

larkfield.name: Larkfield
larkfield.about: A plains-style village on the High Meadow's north-east top (meadow, y 116-119), built (not generated): Jonah's village. From day 4500 a torch stands on every sturdy top in the 90 x 90 box and Jonah's plot is a 9 x 9 square of torches. Every block is 181+ from Dog Hill's D and 185+ from Hushwell's well (outside Dog on the Hill's, Good Boy's and Light Sleeper's render distance); from D the north-east rim's roofs and torches show over the plateau's edge, south-west, 185-190 blocks out.

stamps.what: a torch on every sturdy top in the 90 x 90 box (about 6,000-6,300): fences, roofs, hay, Jonah's 9 x 9 plot. Permanent: from Dog Hill at night the High Meadow's north-east rim glows on the south-west skyline, 185-190 blocks out (needs renderDistance 13+ there). Needs Larkfield's houses as pieces first (Six Thousand Torches' claim of its pieces); on day 4500 itself the story dresses the box (its own skip list, and none in its flashback)

larkfield.status: claimed 2026-11-11 by six_thousand_torches (pieces to add before building)

highwall.name: Highwall
highwall.about: The walled village on a snowy plateau in the middle of the White (y 133-141, snowy plains), 40 blocks from the line of the old road between Frostgate and Ravenford: a square stone-brick wall 40 high on day 3700 (old Tomas adds one block a morning), no gate; outside its north side a player's trading hall, 12 x 52, running north on level ground. The wall's top (~y 175) stands over the White for kilometres: the road's landmark. Built by the story (wall, village, hall). No rendered Short within 450 blocks (Ravenford is 452 west, Frostgate 812 east).
highwall.story_builds: the wall, the village inside it and the trading hall are the story's set (stories/wall_grows/set.md, origin the plaza bell at the claim's at). The wall is 40 high on day 3700 and grows one block a morning while Tomas keeps at it; a later story that shows it must show it at 40 or more (never lower), and none may show it before day 3660

gullwick.name: Gullwick
gullwick.about: A shore hamlet on the low headland west of Leo's lagoon, over the world's only stronghold (never said): the library hut, and a dock (the origin is its end, flush at sea level) pointing north-west across 92 blocks of open cold ocean (never frozen) to Grandma's island. Leo's House is 100 blocks east across the lagoon.
gullwick.story_builds: the dock (12 long, flush at sea level, pointing north-west at the island), the library hut ~20 blocks inland, the shingle shore, the empty oak boat: the_walk's set. The stronghold's pieces (-2313..-2272, -600..-534) run under the headland: never dig here on screen

grandmas_island.name: Grandma's Island
grandmas_island.about: A natural sand-and-grass islet (13 x 17, at sea level) in the cold ocean north-west of Gullwick's dock, 92 blocks out: Grandma's cottage (one lit window facing the dock) and her boat on its beach since about day 350. The nearest true island to the stronghold (55 blocks west of its pieces).
grandmas_island.story_builds: Grandma's cottage (one 3 x 2 glass-pane window facing the dock, lit) and her boat on the beach: the_walk's set, since about day 350
